auth.title: Authentication
auth.snippet:
There are four ways to authenticate with Firecrawl. Each one bills the team that owns the credential and gives access to the same features, so the choice depends on who holds the credential and which interface you call.
## Which should I use?
| You are building | Use | Endpoint | Credential | How it ends |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Your own code calling the REST API for your team | API key | `https://api.firecrawl.dev/v2/...` | `Authorization: Bearer fc-...` | Delete the key in [API keys](https://www.firecrawl.dev/app/api-keys). |
| An MCP client you configure yourself | Hosted MCP with an API key | `https://mcp.firecrawl.dev/v2/mcp` | `Authorization: Bearer fc-...` header in the client config | Delete the key. |
| A connector such as ChatGPT or Claude, or an MCP client with browser sign-in | MCP OAuth | `https://mcp.firecrawl.dev/v2/mcp-oauth` | Handled by the client. Each connection gets its own key. | Revoke it under [Connected apps in Settings](https://www.firecrawl.dev/app/settings?tab=mcp). |
| An app where each user connects their own Firecrawl account | OAuth for apps | `https://api.firecrawl.dev/v2/...` | `Authorization: Bearer fco_...` access token. Each connection gets its own key. | Your app revokes it, or the user revokes it under Connected apps. |

A few REST endpoints also work with no credential at all, so you can try Firecrawl before you have a key. See No API key (keyless).
## API key
Create a key in the [dashboard](https://www.firecrawl.dev/app/api-keys) and send it on every request as `Authorization: Bearer fc-YOUR-API-KEY`. The SDKs take it as `apiKey`. A key has full access to the team that owns it, so keep it on your server. See [Key restrictions](/features/key-restrictions) to limit what a key can do.
## Hosted MCP with an API key
Point your MCP client at `https://mcp.firecrawl.dev/v2/mcp` and add the API key as a bearer token in the client config. Setup for each client is in [Add an API key](/mcp-server/keyless#add-an-api-key).
## MCP OAuth
Point your MCP client at `https://mcp.firecrawl.dev/v2/mcp-oauth`. The client opens a browser, the user signs in and picks a team, and Firecrawl creates a dedicated key for that connection. The client never sees the key. The native ChatGPT and Claude connectors use this flow automatically. Tokens from this flow work only on the MCP server, not on the REST API. See [MCP sign-in](/mcp-server/oauth).
## OAuth for apps
Send the user through Firecrawl’s OAuth flow with `resource=https://api.firecrawl.d

auth.title: OAuth for apps
auth.snippet:
Firecrawl runs an OAuth 2.1 authorization server. Your app sends the user to Firecrawl, the user signs in and picks a team, and your app gets an access token it can use on the Firecrawl REST API in place of an API key. Usage is billed to the team the user picked. Each connection gets its own API key, created by Firecrawl and never shown to your app. The user can see and revoke the connection under Connected apps in Settings, and deleting another key in the dashboard doesn’t affect it.

Overview
| | |
|---|---|
| Discovery | `https://www.firecrawl.dev/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server` |
| Authorization endpoint | `https://www.firecrawl.dev/api/oauth/authorize` |
| Token endpoint | `https://www.firecrawl.dev/api/oauth/token` |
| Revocation endpoint | `https://www.firecrawl.dev/api/oauth/revoke` |
| Registration endpoint | `https://www.firecrawl.dev/api/oauth/register` |
| Resource (audience) | `https://api.firecrawl.dev/` |
| Grant types | `authorization_code`, `refresh_token` |
| PKCE | Required, `S256` only |
| Client authentication | `none` (public clients, no client secret) |
| Access token lifetime | 1 hour, prefix `fco_` |
| Refresh token lifetime | 90 days, prefix `fcr_`, single use |
##
​
Scopes
| Scope | Grants |
|---|---|
| `firecrawl:global` | Full access to the Firecrawl REST API on the chosen team, using that team’s credits. This is the default when `scope` is omitted. |
| `offline_access` | Tells the user on the consent screen that your app stays connected until they revoke it. Requires `firecrawl:global`. |
A token can do anything an API key on that team can do. Request only what you need and keep tokens on your server.
##
​
Register your app
Your app needs a `client_id`. There are two ways to get one, and neither needs approval from Firecrawl.
- Dynamic Client Registration
- Client ID Metadata Document
Register once with [RFC 7591](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc7591) and store the `client_id` it returns.
```
curl -X POST https://www.firecrawl.dev/api/oauth/register \
-H "Content-Type: application/json" \
-d '{
"client_name": "Acme Builder",
"redirect_uris": ["https://acme.example/oauth/firecrawl/callback"],
"grant_types": ["authorization_code", "refresh_token"],
"token_endpoint_auth_method": "none"
}'
```
The `client_name` is what users see on the consent screen.
Host a JSON metadata document at an HTTPS URL you control and use that URL as your `client_id`. Firecrawl fetches it during authorization, so you can update your name and r

auth.title: Introduction
auth.snippet:
All requests use the following base URL:
```
https://api.firecrawl.dev
```
##
​
Authentication
Requests need an `Authorization` header with your API key, except on the keyless endpoints described below:
```
Authorization: Bearer fc-YOUR-API-KEY
```
You can find your API key in the [Firecrawl dashboard](https://www.firecrawl.dev/app/api-keys). A few endpoints, including `/v2/scrape`, `/v2/search` and `/v2/parse`, also work without a key, with limits. To call them keyless, leave the `Authorization` header out entirely, because a header with an empty token returns `401`. See [No API key (keyless)](/authentication#no-api-key-keyless) for the full list. To let users connect their own Firecrawl account to your app instead, use [OAuth for apps](/oauth). [Authentication](/authentication) compares every option. If you are an agent without an API key, start with [Get credentials](/ai-onboarding#get-credentials). If your platform supports WorkOS ID-JAG, use [`auth.md`](https://www.firecrawl.dev/auth.md) for registration instructions.

auth.title: firecrawl.dev/auth.md
auth.snippet:
You are an agent. Firecrawl supports agentic registration for WorkOS ID-JAG identity assertions: discover -> register -> call API. Follow the steps in order; do not skip ahead.
Firecrawl currently supports one registration method:
- `identity_assertion` with `assertion_type: "urn:ietf:params:oauth:token-type:id-jag"`
- `requested_credential_type: "api_key"`
- Credentials are Firecrawl API keys used as bearer tokens.
Firecrawl does not currently support anonymous registration, verified-email registration, claim flows, or `access_token` issuance through `/agent/auth`. Credential revocation is supported but provider-driven (initiated by WorkOS); agents never call it — see [Revocation](#revocation) below.
This is the direct WorkOS ID-JAG registration flow for identity-aware agents. If you need a human to sign in through the browser, install Firecrawl tooling, or save `FIRECRAWL_API_KEY` into a project, use `https://www.firecrawl.dev/agent-onboarding/SKILL.md` instead.
## Step 1 - Discover
Discovery is two hops. On cloud Firecrawl, an unauthenticated call that `https://api.firecrawl.dev` refuses carries `WWW-Authenticate: Bearer resource_metadata="https://www.firecrawl.dev/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource"`: a `401` on an endpoint that needs a key, or a `403` or `429` when the keyless free tier refuses the call. Search, scrape and parse can succeed without a key, so a `200` carries no header. Fetch that URL when the header is present. If you do not have the header in hand, use the conventional metadata URL below.
### 1a. Fetch the Protected Resource Metadata
```http
GET https://www.firecrawl.dev/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource
```
Expected response shape:
```json
{
"resource": "https://api.firecrawl.dev/",
"resource_name": "Firecrawl API",
"resource_logo_uri": "https://www.firecrawl.dev/brand/firecrawl-logo.png",
"authorization_servers": ["https://www.firecrawl.dev"],
"scopes_supported": ["firecrawl:global"],
"bearer_methods_supported": ["header"],
"agent_auth_uri": "https://www.firecrawl.dev/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server"
}
```
Use `resource` as the `aud` when minting an ID-JAG for Firecrawl. Send issued credentials with `Authorization: Bearer <credential>`.
### 1b. Fetch the Authorization Server Metadata
```http
GET https://www.firecrawl.dev/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server
```
The response includes this `agent_auth` block:
```json
{
"agent_auth": {
"skill": "https://www.firecrawl.dev/auth.md",
"register_uri": "https://www.

auth.title: Authentication
auth.snippet:
Authentication
The Firecrawl API uses API keys to authenticate requests. All API requests must include your API key in the Authorization header.
##
​
Getting Your API Key
1
Create an Account
Sign up for a free account at [firecrawl.dev](https://firecrawl.dev).
2
Access Your Dashboard
After signing up, log in to your dashboard.
3
Generate an API Key
Navigate to the API Keys section in your dashboard and click “Create New API Key”.
4
Copy and Store Securely
Copy your API key immediately. It will start with `fc-` followed by a unique string.
**Keep your API key secure!** Your API key carries many privileges, so be sure to keep it secure. Do not share your secret API key in publicly accessible areas such as GitHub, client-side code, or any other public forums.
##
​
Using Your API Key
All API requests must include your API key in the `Authorization` header as a Bearer token:
```
Authorization: Bearer fc-YOUR_API_KEY
```
###
​
REST API
Include the Authorization header in all API requests:
```
curl -X POST 'https://api.firecrawl.dev/v2/scrape' \
-H 'Authorization: Bearer fc-YOUR_API_KEY' \
-H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
-d '{"url": "https://example.com"}'
```
###
​
Python SDK
You can pass your API key directly to the SDK or use an environment variable:
###
​
JavaScript/Node.js SDK
Similar to Python, you can pass the API key directly or use an environment variable:
##
​
Environment Variables
It’s recommended to store your API key in environment variables rather than hardcoding it in your application:
- .env File
- System Environment
- Docker
- CI/CD
Create a `.env` file in your project root:
```
FIRECRAWL_API_KEY=fc-YOUR_API_KEY
```
**Python**: Use `python-dotenv` to load environment variables:
```
from dotenv import load_dotenv
from firecrawl import Firecrawl
load_dotenv()
app = Firecrawl()  # Automatically uses FIRECRAWL_API_KEY from .env
```
**JavaScript**: Use `dotenv` package:
```
import 'dotenv/config';
import Firecrawl from '@mendable/firecrawl-js';
const app = new Firecrawl();  // Automatically uses FIRECRAWL_API_KEY from .env
```

## Use Different Keys
Use different API keys for development, staging, and production environments.

Managing Multiple API Keys
You can create multiple API keys for different purposes:
- **Development**: For local development and testing
- **Staging**: For pre-production environments
- **Production**: For live applications
- **CI/CD**: For automated testing and deployments
To create additional API keys, go to your dashboa

auth.title: firecrawl/skills/firecrawl-build-onboarding/references/auth-flow.md at main · firecrawl/firecrawl
auth.snippet:
# Auth Flow
Use this browser flow when the user does not already have a Firecrawl API key.
## Step 1: Generate auth parameters
```
SESSION_ID=$(openssl rand -hex 32)
CODE_VERIFIER=$(openssl rand -base64 32 | tr '+/' '-_' | tr -d '=\n' | head -c 43)
CODE_CHALLENGE=$(printf '%s' "$CODE_VERIFIER" | openssl dgst -sha256 -binary | openssl base64 -A | tr '+/' '-_' | tr -d '=')
```
## Step 2: Ask the user to open this URL
```
https://www.firecrawl.dev/cli-auth?code_challenge=$CODE_CHALLENGE&source=coding-agent#session_id=$SESSION_ID
```
The user completes the browser authorization flow. If successful, the API key becomes available through the polling endpoint.
## Step 3: Poll for completion
```
POST https://www.firecrawl.dev/api/auth/cli/status
Content-Type: application/json
{"session_id":"$SESSION_ID","code_verifier":"$CODE_VERIFIER"}
```
Responses:
- `{"status":"pending"}` - continue polling
- `{"status":"complete","apiKey":"fc-...","teamName":"..."}`
## Step 4: Save the key
```
echo "FIRECRAWL_API_KEY=fc-..." >> .env
```

access.title: Rate Limits
access.snippet:
The hosted Firecrawl MCP keyless endpoint exposes exactly **Search, Scrape, and Parse** without an API key. Other hosted MCP tools require an account connection or an API key. For official Firecrawl clients, the CLI, SDKs, and REST API, keyless access also includes **Interact**. On Firecrawl Cloud, research, developer, and government search endpoints can also be used without an API key. No other endpoints (crawl, extract, map, batch scrape, etc.) are available without a key. Keyless usage is free and capped per IP address per day by **two limits**, and exceeding either returns a `429`:
- A maximum number of **requests** per day.
- A maximum number of **credits** per day. Operations cost different amounts of credits (for example, Interact and JSON extraction cost more than a basic scrape), so heavier usage reaches the credit cap sooner.
[Sign up for a free API key](https://firecrawl.dev) to get 1,000 credits and higher rate limits at no cost — official clients automatically use your key once it’s configured.

access.title: Billing
access.snippet:
Firecrawl billing is **credit-based**. Every API call that you make consumes credits. The number of credits depends on the endpoint and the options that you use. Your plan gives you a monthly credit allotment. Pay-as-you-go adds more credits when the allotment runs out. For current plan pricing, visit the [Firecrawl pricing page](https://www.firecrawl.dev/pricing).

New accounts start on the free plan. It costs nothing and does not need a card. Here is what it includes:
- **1,000 credits per month.** The allotment resets at the start of each monthly cycle. Unused free credits do not roll over.
- **2 concurrent browsers**, with the same 50,000 maximum queued jobs as the paid self-serve plans.

The free plan does not include pay-as-you-go, so requests return an HTTP 402 once the monthly allotment runs out. See Running Out of Credits. It also does not include credit rollover, a Data Processing Agreement, or Slack support. Support is community support. Scrape, Search and Interact also work with no API key at all, through the keyless free tier, which is capped per IP address per day rather than by a credit allotment. See [Keyless (no API key)](/rate-limits#keyless-no-api-key).

access.title: Partner Credits
access.snippet:
The standard partner offer may include **10,000 free Firecrawl credits**. These credits let you use any Firecrawl endpoint, including [Search](/features/search), [Scrape](/features/scrape), [Crawl](/features/crawl), [Map](/features/map), [Interact](/features/interact), and more. See [Billing](/billing#credits) for how credits are consumed per endpoint.

Partner credits use Firecrawl’s **standard Free Plan limits** unless otherwise stated by the partner offer. This includes the same rate limits and concurrent browser limits as the Free plan. See [Rate Limits](/rate-limits) for the full breakdown of per-plan limits.
## What’s Not Included
The partner offer **does not include** a paid Firecrawl plan or a Hobby Plan upgrade. Your account remains on the Free plan with the associated rate limits and concurrency; you simply receive additional credits to use within that plan.
## Need More?
If you need more credits, higher rate limits, or access to paid-plan features, you can upgrade your Firecrawl account independently at any time:
- Visit the [Firecrawl pricing page](https://www.firecrawl.dev/pricing) to compare plans
- Upgrade directly from your [dashboard](https://www.firecrawl.dev/app)
- See [Billing](/billing#plans) for details on available plans and [Pay-as-you-go](/billing#pay-as-you-go)

After 3 months, any unused partner credits are removed from your account. If you have not upgraded to a paid plan, your account remains on the standard Free plan. You can upgrade at any time from the [pricing page](https://www.firecrawl.dev/pricing).

access.title: Firecrawl API Limits and Credits for Developers
access.snippet:
The [Firecrawl](https://www.firecrawl.dev/pricing) API is a set of HTTP endpoints that turn web pages into clean, LLM-ready data, and because any HTTP client can call it, you can just as easily trigger it from a workflow tool like [Activepieces](https://www.activepieces.com) as from your own code, and every call spends credits from the account that owns your key.

You get a key from a Firecrawl account, created in the dashboard, and send it as a bearer token with each request.
Which endpoints, credit allowances and concurrency limits your plan includes is set on the pricing page and in the docs, and both change. Read them on the day you build, not from this article.
Everything below works on Activepieces' free plan. [Start without code or a credit card.](https://cloud.activepieces.com/sign-up?ap_cta=blog_anchor&ref=%2Fblog%2Ffirecrawl-api-limits-and-credits-for-developers)
## Authentication and a Minimal Working Request
Send your API key as a Bearer token in the Authorization header, because Firecrawl authenticates every call that way. One leaked or missing key is the difference between a working job and a wall of rejected requests.

You are billed in credits and capped per plan:
- Free gets 1,000 credits a month: - Hobby gets 5,000 credits a month
- A 10,000-page job fails on both: before concurrency even matters

Set your page count against the monthly credits on [Firecrawl's pricing page](https://www.firecrawl.dev/pricing): 1,000 on Free, 5,000 on Hobby, 100,000 on Standard, 500,000 on Growth and 1,000,000 on Scale.

| Plan | Monthly credits | Concurrent requests | /scrape per min | /crawl per min | /search per min | /map per min |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Free | 1,000 | 2 | 10 | 2 | 10 | 10 |
| Hobby | 5,000 | 5 | 100 | 15 | 50 | 100 |
| Standard | 100,000 | 25 | 500 | 100 | 100 | 500 |
| Growth | 500,000 | 50 | 5,000 | 250 | 2,500 | 5,000 |
| Scale | 1,000,000 | 100 | not published | not published | not published | not published |

Is the Firecrawl API free to use? There's a free tier, but it's an allowance, not an open door.
Once its credits or concurrency are spent, requests stop or queue, so treat it as a place to test against a handful of URLs, not to run a production job. Check the pricing page for what it includes today.

mcp.snippet:
# Firecrawl MCP Server
A Model Context Protocol (MCP) server that brings [Firecrawl](https://github.com/firecrawl/firecrawl), the context API for AI agents, to MCP-compatible clients: search, scrape, and interact with the live web and get back clean Markdown or structured data.
> Big thanks to [@vrknetha](https://github.com/vrknetha), [@knacklabs](https://www.knacklabs.ai) for the initial implementation!
## Features
- Search the web, optionally with full page content for each result
- Search indexes for developer sources (GitHub issues, merged pull requests, READMEs, and docs), US government sources, and scientific papers (PubMed, bioRxiv, medRxiv, arXiv)
- Scrape any URL into clean Markdown or structured JSON
- Parse PDFs and documents
- Crawl a site for content from many pages, or map it to discover its URLs
- Interact with pages in a real browser: click, type, fill forms, and navigate dynamic pages
- Run Agent jobs for multi-source research that returns structured data
- Monitor pages and get notified when their content changes
- Check current and historical Firecrawl credit usage
- Automatic retries and rate limiting
- Cloud and self-hosted support
- SSE support
> Play around with [our MCP Server on MCP.so's playground](https://mcp.so/playground?server=firecrawl-mcp-server) or on [Klavis AI](https://www.klavis.ai/mcp-servers).
## When to Use This Server
- Use `firecrawl_scrape` when you have a known URL and want its content as markdown or as JSON matching a schema you supply.
- Use `firecrawl_map` when you need to discover URLs on a site without fetching their content.
- Use `firecrawl_crawl` when you need content from many pages under a site; set `limit`, `includePaths`/`excludePaths`, or `maxDiscoveryDepth` to bound it.
- Use `firecrawl_search` when you're starting from a query rather than a URL and want ranked web results. Results carry excerpts; fetch full pages with `firecrawl_scrape` on the URLs you need. `scrapeOptions` fetches every result's page in the same call and bills each as a scrape, so keep it for the full text of a few results (the search-only endpoint never fetches content).
- Use `firecrawl_interact` when a page needs a click, type, or navigate action before you can read it: pass a `url` for a fresh page or a `scrapeId` to continue on one you already scraped.
- Use the `firecrawl_monitor_*` tools when the same page needs to be checked on a recurring schedule with diffs and change alerts, rather than fetched once.
- Use `firecrawl_cre

mcp.title: Developers & MCP
mcp.snippet:
Firecrawl’s MCP server connects to Claude Desktop, Cursor, and other Model Context Protocol clients so your assistant can pull live documentation, discover site structures, and extract structured data on demand.
##
​
Start with a Template
## MCP Server Firecrawl
Official MCP server - Search, scrape, and interact with the web from Claude Desktop, Cursor, and other MCP clients
## Open Lovable
Build complete applications from any website instantly
**Get started with MCP in minutes.** Follow our [setup guide](https://github.com/firecrawl/firecrawl-mcp-server#installation) to integrate Firecrawl into Claude Desktop or Cursor.
##
​
How It Works
Integrate Firecrawl directly into your AI coding workflow through Model Context Protocol. Once configured, your AI assistant gains access to a set of Firecrawl web tools it can call on your behalf:
| Tool | What it does |
|---|---|
| **Scrape** | Extract content or structured data from a single URL |
| **Batch Scrape** | Extract content from multiple known URLs in parallel |
| **Map** | Discover all indexed URLs on a website |
| **Crawl** | Walk a site section and extract content from every page |
| **Search** | Search the web and optionally extract content from results |

Currently, Claude Desktop and Cursor have native MCP support. More AI assistants are adding support regularly. You can also use the MCP SDK to build custom integrations.
Yes. VS Code supports MCP natively: run **MCP: Add Server** from the Command Palette, choose **HTTP**, and enter `https://mcp.firecrawl.dev/v2/mcp`. To add it by hand, put Firecrawl under `mcpServers` in `~/.copilot/mcp-config.json` for all your workspaces, or in `.mcp.json` at the workspace root to share it with your team:
```

```
mcp.title: Agent Development Kit (ADK)
mcp.snippet:
Connect Google’s Agent Development Kit (ADK) to Firecrawl through the Model Context Protocol (MCP) so your agents can search, scrape, crawl, and map the web for clean context.
## Overview
Firecrawl provides an MCP server that seamlessly integrates with Google’s ADK, enabling your agents to efficiently scrape, crawl, and extract structured data from any website. The integration supports both cloud-based and self-hosted Firecrawl instances with streamable HTTP for optimal performance.
## Features
- Efficient web scraping, crawling, and content discovery from any website
- Advanced search capabilities and intelligent content extraction
- Autonomous web research with the Firecrawl agent
- Browser interaction, file parsing, and change monitoring
- Flexible deployment (cloud-based or self-hosted)
- Optimized for modern web environments with streamable HTTP support
## Prerequisites
- Obtain an API key for Firecrawl from [firecrawl.dev](https://firecrawl.dev)
- Install Google ADK with MCP support: `pip install "google-adk[mcp]"`
## Setup
```
import os
from google.adk.agents.llm_agent import Agent
from google.adk.tools.mcp_tool.mcp_session_manager import StreamableHTTPConnectionParams
from google.adk.tools.mcp_tool.mcp_toolset import MCPToolset
FIRECRAWL_API_KEY = os.environ["FIRECRAWL_API_KEY"]
root_agent = Agent(
model="gemini-3.8-flash",
name="firecrawl_agent",
description='A helpful assistant for scraping websites with Firecrawl',
instruction='Help the user search for website content',
tools=[
MCPToolset(
connection_params=StreamableHTTPConnectionParams(
url="https://mcp.firecrawl.dev/v2/mcp",
headers={"Authorization": f"Bearer {FIRECRAWL_API_KEY}"},
),
)
],
)
```
Set `FIRECRAWL_API_KEY` in the environment that starts ADK. Do not put its value in agent prompts, source control, or the MCP URL. The local MCP package requires Node.js 22 or newer.
```

mcp.title: Firecrawl MCP in ChatGPT: Web Scraping and Search Inside Your Conversations
mcp.snippet:
On September 10, 2025, OpenAI shipped full Model Context Protocol support in ChatGPT and called it Developer Mode. I was thrilled because ChatGPT's built-in browsing has been buggy for as long as I've used it.
It struggles with JavaScript-rendered content, can't handle authentication, returns summaries when you need raw data, and formats results inconsistently.

Firecrawl MCP solves this by connecting ChatGPT directly to Firecrawl's web scraping and search tools. Instead of relying on ChatGPT's basic browsing, you get an agent-ready toolkit that handles complex site requirements, renders dynamic content, and extracts structured data on demand.

If you’re unfamiliar, the Model Context Protocol (MCP) is a standardized method for AI models to interact with external tools and data, [introduced by Anthropic](https://www.anthropic.com/news/model-context-protocol) in late 2024.
MCP uses lightweight [JSON-RPC 2.0](https://www.jsonrpc.org/specification) for message exchange and defines standard formats for requests, responses, and errors.
The clever part is that it solves the m×n integration problem. Instead of every AI client needing custom integrations with every tool, each side only needs to implement the protocol once. Think of it as a universal adapter that lets different systems communicate using a common language.
ChatGPT's [Developer Mode](https://help.openai.com/en/articles/12584461-developer-mode-apps-and-full-mcp-connectors-in-chatgpt-beta) turns the desktop into a full MCP client. Once enabled, you can connect to any compatible MCP server and use its tools directly in your conversations. This includes both read operations (fetching data) and write operations (creating, updating, or deleting data in connected systems).
## What is Firecrawl MCP?
[Firecrawl](https://firecrawl.dev/) is a web scraping and search API for AI agents that handles the messy parts of using live websites: JavaScript rendering, pagination, rate limiting, and converting pages to clean markdown. The [Firecrawl MCP server](https://github.com/firecrawl/firecrawl-mcp-server) exposes this functionality through MCP, making it available to any compatible AI client.
